This is second Criminal Appeal under Section 14-A (2) of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act by appellant who has been arrested by Police on 19.6.2022 in connection with Crime No.472/2022, registered at Police Station MIG, Indore concerning offence under Sections 420, 468, 471, 201, 34 of IPC and under Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and under Section 3/5 of M.P. Freedom of Religion Act against the order dated 23.1.2023, passed by the learned Special Judge (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Indore, whereby the prayer for grant of regular bail has been rejected.

sentences.text: 3. First Criminal Appeal No.9500/2022 was dismissed as withdrawn by order dated 11.11.2022.
4. As per the prosecution, a report was lodged by the prosecutrix to the effect that she had met one Mahesh Yadav in front of Thana Palasiya who had asked her to stay away from Muslim boys.
On 13.11.2018, she had made a report against one Shahbaz Khan.
Mahesh Yadav took her to a flat in Baldev Apartment and kept her there.
After 4-5 days he came and asked her to enter into a compromise with Shahbaz which she eventually did.
Mahesh then took her to a flat in a Multiplex and she started residing there.
He used to come often to her and they developed physical relationship.
She then went along with him and his friends to Mahakal Mandir, Ujjain and got married according to Hindu rites.
Thereafter they shifted to Rameshwari apartment in Indore.
On 03.07.2021 during check up her Doctor told her that she is pregnant.
She was not well hence Mahesh got her some tablets and made her consume them.
Thereafter he revealed that he is not Mahesh but is in fact a Muslim and his real name is Basil Mansoori the appellant.
He stated that they shall have to get married according to Muslim rites.
She refused but he, his father Sayeed Ahmed and uncle Rizwan, got her married to Basil according to Muslim rites.
After some time they got her religion changed from Hindu to Muslim in the flat at Rameshwari apartment.
Thereafter she fell ill and on 20.08.2021 Basil took her to a hospital accompanied by the other co-accused and got her abortion done.
After coming back she was informed that her abortion has been done and she can do whatever she wants.
On 28.05.2022, Basil disappeared saying that he is going to Ajmer and never returned, after which she lodged a missing person report in his regard at Ajmer.
The co-accused Sayeed then asked her to take Rs.10,00,000/- from him and to leave his son alone.
On lodging of the report by the prosecutrix, appellant has been implicated for the present offence.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
Subsequent to withdrawal of the previous appeal the prosecutrix has been examined before the trial court and she has not supported the prosecution case in any manner and has been declared hostile.
She has categorically stated that the appellant has not committed any wrongful act upon her and has not forced her to change her religion.
It is also submitted that the appellant is in custody since 19.6.2022 and the trial is still likely to take time for its conclusion.
Since the prosecutrix has admitted that she had married the appellant and is his wife, his further incarceration is not desirable.
Trial is still likely to take time for its conclusion.

On such grounds,
prayer for grant of bail to the appellant has been made.

5. The aforesaid prayer has been opposed by learned counsel for the State submitting that in view of the allegations levelled against the appellant and the material collected by the prosecution against him, he is not entitled to be released on bail merely on the basis of statement of the prosecutrix.
6. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary as well as statement of the prosecutrix.
7. Subsequent to withdrawal of the previous appeal the prosecutrix has been examined before the trial court and she has not supported the prosecution case in any manner and has been declared hostile.
She has categorically stated that appellant did not commit any wrongful act upon her and did not force her to change her religion.

Applicant is in custody since 19.6.2022 and the possibility of the trial still taking a long time for its conclusion cannot be ruled out.
Thus in my opinion, the appellant deserves to be enlarged on bail.

8. Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the appeal filed by the appellant is allowed and the impugned order dated 23.1.2022, passed by the learned Special Judge (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Indore is hereby set aside.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The appellant is directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the Court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3)
Cr.P.C.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial, however, in case of bail jump, it shall become ineffective.
C.c. as per rules.
